because: ran the discriminating test on Node 25.2.1 with config.testMatch set to the README's recommended '[1-9][0-9]* passed'. BOTH routes make a vanished oracle green: (1) with the pattern as a real node option, a pattern matching nothing still reports the FILE as one passing test ('ok 1 - <file>', '# pass 1', exit 0) — the conjectured candidate, confirmed; (2) and there is a second, worse route nobody would notice — node stops parsing its own options at the first positional, so a config.test of [node, --test, <glob>, --test-name-pattern] passes the flag to the SCRIPT, the filter is silently inert, the WHOLE suite runs and passes, and every claim goes green regardless of what it names. Either way testMatch is satisfied, so the README's advice does not protect node:test projects.
